description: Techniques the awwwards skill loop can use to understand websites — per domain. Grown by the skill-memory flywheel: a finding that proposes a better technique gets promoted here by a human PR. Each entry: id, domain, when (when to use it), how (concrete steps/commands), source (where it came from).

video-understanding.summary: From recording to model-ready motion context. Field consensus 2025-2026: scene detection FIRST, keyframes per scene, adaptive any-k budget, then structured context to the model. Our tile-per-element doctrine is the special case for short UI loops; layered analysis + superprompt hand-off extends it beyond in-session builds.

techniques.when: Rebuilding any multi-section page from a reference (see skills/awwwards-section-loop).
how: analyze_page_structure band map = build order; one giant band (5000px+) means collapsed sections - switch to explicit class/id selectors per real section
capture_component per section in band order; selector ladder: class/id > role attr > tag names (real sites often lack <header>)
verify_build per band after each section builds - read ONLY that band's score; iterate until it passes; LOCK the section before starting the next
Shared WebGL/canvas across bands = page does not slice - capture_pose_3d for that region as ONE unit
Final whole-page verify_build = coherence pass (spacing rhythm, easing family, scroll continuity), fixed at token level not by re-opening locked sections
techniques.source: Recreation-kit dogfooding 2026-10-17: estherwong.fun (header tag miss, 2-band map) + neutomni.com (20631px collapsed band, Webflow selector ladder)

techniques.when: Before tiling any recording longer than ~20s or with multiple distinct animations (preloader → scroll → transition).
how: ffmpeg -i ref.webm -vf "select='gt(scene,0.3)',showinfo" -vsync vfr keyframes/%03d.png  # scene-change keyframes
Alternative low-threshold pass for UI micro-motion: select='gt(scene,0.08)' (UI cuts are subtle vs film cuts)
Segment the recording at scene boundaries, then treat each segment as its own study passage
techniques.source: arXiv scene-detection survey (2025); Mixpeek production pipeline (2026); K-frames any-k selection (OpenReview)

techniques.when: Long recordings that exceed the tile budget — decide WHICH frames deserve model context instead of uniform sampling.
how: One keyframe per detected scene (the scene's first stable frame)
Spend the remaining frame budget on scenes that contain the element under study
Feed keyframes WITH timestamps — timing is the data for easing inference

techniques.when: Easing/overlap matters inside one scene (the existing 2-6fps tile rule, now scoped to the scene segment).
how: ffmpeg -ss <scene-start> -to <scene-end> -i ref.webm -vf "fps=6,scale=480:-1,tile=6x4" scene-tile.jpg
Re-tile finer only for the frames where motion actually changes

techniques.when: After the motion inventory, before building — and always when the study output is a hand-off (another agent, an article, a future session) instead of an in-session build.
how: Sweep the tiles through five lenses beyond motion: story (purpose, arc, section order), layout (grids, sticky zones, nav/footer anatomy), visual design (type scale, palette, surfaces, texture), technical rebuild (which mechanism serves each effect), a11y + performance (reduced motion, touch states, lazy loading, pixel-ratio caps)
A lens finding that changes the build gets its own inventory row or build note

For hand-offs, compile inventory + lenses into one paste-ready superprompt: final build + reference boundary, asset map, global design language, section-by-section anatomy (purpose/layout/animation/interactions/scroll/library/reduced-motion), anti-patterns
Bar: the prompt must be long enough to rebuild the interaction without seeing the original video — no vague taste words, only mechanisms and numbers
techniques.source: video-to-superprompt skill (layered analysis + superprompt quality bar), merged into the motion-study loop 2026-09-19

motion-detection.summary: What a live site tells you about its motion stack BEFORE recording — fingerprint the libraries, diff the computed styles, poll the transforms.

techniques.when: Capture phase, before recording — know which animation stack you are studying so build-side patterns match (GSAP vs Motion vs CSS scroll-timeline).
how: In captured HTML: script srcs matching /gsap|ScrollTrigger|ScrollMagic|locomotive|motion|lenis|barba/i
Inline transforms set by GSAP (style="transform: translate(...) matrix(...)") on scroll-coupled elements
CSS scroll-timeline / animation-timeline / scroll() functions → native CSS scroll-driven animation (uneven browser support — annnimate 2026)
techniques.source: Blink.new clone-from-URL approach; annnimate GSAP-vs-CSS 2026; motion.dev comparisons

techniques.when: Micro-interactions: hover states that a screenshot cannot show. Captures the EXACT style delta instead of eyeballing film frames.
how: For each interactive element (cursor:pointer discovery, as in record-scrollthrough.mjs):
const rest = getComputedStyle(el); el.dispatchEvent(new MouseEvent('mouseover', {bubbles:true}));
await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 700)); const hover = getComputedStyle(el);
diff rest vs hover on: transform, opacity, color, background, box-shadow, letter-spacing, filter, clip-path
Record the diff per element — this IS the micro-interaction inventory
techniques.source: record-scrollthrough.mjs virtual-cursor pattern (ours) + computed-style diffing standard practice

techniques.when: Scroll-scrubbed animations where per-frame tiles cannot separate scroll-position coupling from time-based easing.
how: During the stepped scroll, rAF-poll target elements: getComputedStyle(el).transform sampled per step
A transform that changes ONLY with scroll = scrub-coupled; one that keeps changing after scroll stops = time-based tween
This distinguishes ScrollTrigger scrub:true from scrub-timeline + toggleActions — the #1 rebuild mistake
techniques.source: GSAP ScrollTrigger docs pattern (ours, gsap-scrolltrigger skill)

ui-structure.summary: Structure before pixels. Band maps exist (analyze_page_structure); these extend structure understanding to tokens, rhythm, and overflow.

how: analyze_page_structure on reference AND build; compare count/order/backgrounds/heights; never pad spacer bands

techniques.when: Recreating a reference faithfully — extract the tokens before writing CSS.
how: Palette: sample band backgrounds + dominant colors (ffmpeg palettegen on hero capture, or canvas sampling in page.evaluate)
Type scale: histogram of computed font-sizes + families across headings/body (page.evaluate document.querySelectorAll('*') sample)
Spacing rhythm: computed margins/paddings of section boundaries → find the multiple (8/12/16 grid)

techniques.when: After any responsive build — horizontal overflow at any breakpoint is a structural bug.
how: For each viewport (desktop 1440, mobile 390): document.scrollWidth > window.innerWidth → report offending elements (walk tree for el.getBoundingClientRect().right > innerWidth)
Record the offender + the px — pin shots will show it as asymmetric whitespace

micro-interactions.summary: Small feedback animations — capture the state PAIRS, not just the motion.

how: Screenshot element bounding-box at rest AND at hover (elementHandle.screenshot()), pair them in the inventory
Pair with hover-pair-style-diff for the CSS-level truth

techniques.when: Award sites with custom cursors — invisible in screenshots, disruptive if uncloned.
how: mousemove listener audit: elements moved by rAF against mouse position (transform updated within 50ms of mousemove)
Detect mix-blend-mode: difference / exclusion overlays — the classic custom-cursor signature

images.summary: Image evidence discipline — the doctrine that findings carry proof extends to capture sets.

techniques.when: Design DNA from a hero image when the site's own palette metadata is absent.
how: ffmpeg -i hero.png -vf palettegen=max_colors=8 - > palette.png; sample the PNG
techniques.source: ffmpeg standard; awwwards palette field gaps

techniques.when: QA sets with 13+ pin shots — near-duplicates waste context when reviewing.
how: Perceptual hash (block-mean 8x8 grayscale) per frame; drop frames with hamming distance < 4 from a kept neighbor
Node implementation is ~30 lines, no deps
techniques.source: perceptual hashing standard practice; our QA shot review overhead
